english.html: flamed, went straight to his house to find his wife, threw her upon the bed, telling her that he wished to get her with child of a devil. Which he did, or at least of a son who had the form of a little devil, and who began from the moment he was born to leap and bound <sup class="mk" data-key="u">u</sup>. And if the reader is not content, but further asks the reason why this impression of different forms, according to the conceptions, happens peculiarly to men more than to the other animals: I shall think I answer them sufficiently with Pliny, if I tell them that the quickness of thoughts, the celerity of the understanding and the diversity of minds imprint diverse forms and marks upon men, whereas in the other living souls the conceptions and thoughts are uniform and alike among all, and for each in its kind; and thus, not having this multiplicity of imaginations, forms and representations, they always bring forth their young resembling their sires and dams <sup class="mk" data-key="x">x</sup>. And because also persons, at the instant of the venereal pleasure, are most often occupied with nothing but the pleasure alone, in which they hold the mind without letting it stray to any other thought, it likewise comes about that children are commonly like their parents and progenitors. Whence some of our interpreters of the law determine an old question: if a woman, immediately after the death of her first husband, remarries, and at the end of nine months is delivered, to which of the two husbands the child ought to be adjudged <sup class="mk" data-key="y">y</sup>. For although many adjudge it to the first husband <sup class="mk" data-key="z">z</sup>, precisely because it is to be imputed to the second, who was in too great haste to marry the widow <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>; and others to the second, both because he has longer laboured and cultivated the ground <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>, that is to say, cohabited carnally with the woman, to the effect of this pregnancy, and also because the child was born in his house and during his marriage <sup class="mk" data-key="c">c</sup>; and a third party presume the child to belong to both, just as the law also sometimes takes the conjecture that a slave (who nevertheless can belong wholly to only one) belongs to two masters, and to each entirely <sup class="mk" data-key="d">d</sup>; and there are also some who, on account of the confusion and disturbance of the blood and of the seed <sup class="mk" data-key="e">e</sup>, presume it to be neither the first

uncertain.note: page quality: the leaf is clean, evenly inked and in sharp focus. A brown stain/crease crosses the blank head margin above the running head but touches no type. Faint show-through of the recto is visible below the last body line but is legible as offset, not as text. Nothing is lost to damage or to the crop; the narrow strip of the facing page along the right (gutter) edge has been ignored throughout. The doubts below concern letterforms and compositor's spacing, not legibility.

counts for the reconciler: 40 printed body lines in a single paragraph block; no heading, no ornament, no decorated initial, no foot citation block, no signature, no catchword. 9 markers (u x y z a b c d e), each with a margin note; 9 margin notes, each with a marker.

continues_prev: the page opens mid-sentence with 'chauffé, ſ'en va droit à ſa maiſon' — the tail of a sentence begun on p017, which is not yet transcribed, so the reading rests on the sense alone. continues_next: the last line ends 'eſtre du premier' with no point, so the paragraph runs on to p019.

markers: the printer's alphabet runs u, x, y, z on this page and then restarts at a for the last five citations (a b c d e). Since no earlier a–e occurs on this page, the restarted letters are keyed plainly a, b, c, d, e (no a2), per §4. The marker on lines[4] is the small italic u shown in the §9 worked example; the markers z (lines[27]) and a (lines[29]) are the smallest sorts on the page but are legible at 4x.

the key letter printed at the head of this note looks more like an italic n than a u at 4x (the left stroke curves into the first shoulder). Read as u from the alphabet position and from the body marker, which is unambiguously u. Not included in lines, per §9.

the numeral is set as x plus a single y-with-diaeresis sort, the italic font's 'ij' sort; transcribed 'xij' per §2 and the house practice used on p044 ('xxviij'). Same sort in margin_notes[1].lines[1] ('vij', 'xij'), margin_notes[4].lines[0] ('l. ij.') and margin_notes[7].lines[0] ('ſocij').

the word 'liure' is broken across the two lines of the note as 'li.' + 'ure'. The mark after 'li' sits on the baseline and is the same size as the abbreviation points in 'liur.de' and 'S.Aug.'; it is NOT the margin font's line-end hyphen, which is a short raised slanted stroke (compare 'les au-' and 'au ver-' at 5x). Transcribed as a point, so the line is 'Pline au li.' and not 'Pline au li-'.
printed 'ure vÿ. e.xÿ.' with 'e.xÿ.' set tight; the space after the point is supplied per §1. 'e.' is the abbreviation for the chapter (Pliny, Nat. hist. vii. 12).

the z citation is printed as a continuation of the y note's block, with no blank line between them: 'libe. & poſt.' ends the y note and the next line opens with the key z. The split between the two notes is therefore an editorial judgement — 'libe. & poſt.' ( = de liberis et poſthumis) completes the Digest title of the y citation, so it is assigned to y.
e+n read at 7x (closed eye and mid-bar of the italic e, as in 'en la l.' of note y); A read 'an'. = in VI (Liber Sextus). Reconciled, see decisions.

sic: the word broken as 'au ver-' + 'ſieule' gives 'verſieule' where the sense wants 'verſicule'. The third sort is an e (closed bowl with a mid bar at 9x), not a c. Transcribed as printed, not emended.

no point is visible after the initial l of this citation, unlike 'l. filium.' and 'l. duo ſocij.' in the notes below, where the point is clear. A very faint speck may be present. Transcribed without the point; reader A may read 'l. Titia. D.'
sic: the second word is d+o at 6x (a closed round bowl, no mid bar), where the sense wants 'de' ( = D. de hæredibus inſtituendis). Transcribed as printed.

beside_line values are approximate. The margin is crowded and set on a tighter leading than the body, so several notes begin a line or two above the body line that carries their marker (the y note starts beside lines[21], its marker is on lines[26]; the z note beside lines[25], marker on lines[27]; the a note beside lines[28], marker on lines[29]; the e note beside lines[37], marker on lines[39]). Where a note's first line falls between two body lines I have chosen the nearer baseline; the reconciler should not treat a one-line disagreement here as a substantive diff.

there is no foot citation block, no signature and no catchword: all nine citations fit in the outer margin, and the lower quarter of the leaf is blank. A small hooked pen stroke in dark ink (roughly the shape of a long s or a reversed c, about 6 mm high) stands alone in the blank outer margin at the very foot of the page, well outside the type area, with two small ink specks to its right. It is manuscript or offset, not type, and is not a signature — this is a verso, and the mark is on the outer, not the inner, side. Not recorded as an ornament.
